text.p: The former comptroller of a United Nations area synagogue whose membership includes prominent political figures was arrested Thursday for bank fraud, federal officials said.

Michael Kleinberg, 39, of Manhattan was charged for his alleged role in an embezzlement scheme that targeted Sutton Place Synagogue, which is is also known as the Jewish Centre of the United Nations. The synagogue is believed to have lost at least $500,000 in the scheme, which allegedly lasted from 1993 until August of this year.
Kleinberg, who had been the comptroller for the 900-member synagogue for six years, was fired in August.

He pleaded not guilty before a federal magistrate judge later Thursday and was released on a $100,000 personal recognisance bond. If convicted he faces a possible maximum sentence of 30 years in prison and a $1 million fine.

His lawyer, Michael Handwerker, said that his client denies the accusations and believes he is being made a scapegoat. He said that he had hired a forensic accountant and private investigator to study the allegations.
"This is a very high-powered, well-to-do synagogue," Handwerker said. "It seems to me somebody was not paying attention."

The complaint, filed in Manhattan federal court, said that Kleinberg was responsible for the synagogue's computerized general ledger system, the preparation of checks for signature by authorised persons and the withdrawal of cash from the synagogues's checking account.
The synagogue allegedly lost in excess of $500,000 through unauthorised withdrawals from the checking account.

In June 1996 ,Kleinberg allegedly asked a synagogue employee to discard two large boxes of papers fitting the description of the synagogue's check stubs and asked the employee not to let the synagogue's executive director know.

It was also alleged that in July, the synagogue's auditors told Kleinberg they would be conducting an audit of the books, records and the general ledger. Several days later, the synagogue's general ledger had been deleted from the computer system and most of the books and records were destroyed, the complaint alleged.
Kleinberg was the only person at the synagogue who had access to the computerized general ledger and who kept custody of the books and records, the complaint alleged.
